source_message.text:
Hi Jessica,

Thank you for your interest in this project! Based on our review of your profile and the sample writings, we think you might be a great fit for this project.

A little about us: We are Vibrant Publishers, an international publishing company based out of Colorado, USA. We publish practical and industry-focused books.

To explore our collection and the types of books we publish, feel free to explore our website: <https://www.vibrantpublishers.com>

This project is specifically for our Job Interview Questions Series. Job Interview Questions Series is aimed at making the interview preparation process easy and quick, and helping individuals to develop confidence in acing any interview round.

As our job description specified, we are currently in the process of creating the second edition of our title, Leadership Interview Questions You’ll Most Likely be Asked. The book is created specially for professionals, new managers, individuals who are transitioning into leadership roles, and experienced leaders shifting roles.

To give you a clear context, we have some specific ideas for the second edition of this title. However, we would also like your professional and expert opinion on the same. As the expert here, we would love to know what you think of our suggested revisions and tell us how practical they are. Once we are clear on the revisions, we can decide on the requirements and project timelines accordingly.

For the second edition, please note the following additions:

1\. New chapters: Pre-interview preparation, questions for remote and hybrid leadership roles, questions that individuals can ask the interviewer, use of AI in interview preparation, and questions specifically for individuals who are transitioning into leadership roles for the first time.

2\. Answer layers: Along with the standard answers, there will be more sections, like the interviewer's intent, common red flags, how to frame the answer, and the ideal answer/sample answer.

3\. Additional options: Company matrix answers & answer frameworks (like STAR)
Additionally, as part of our standard process, we would also like to request a short test before the project starts. The test is required because it helps us understand your expertise, writing style, and structuring abilities. On the same note, the test will also give you a preview of what it would be like to work on this project.

We are sharing a document with you, which has all the instructions for the test.

Please go through the shared document and share your responses accordingly. It would be great if you could provide a timeline by which you will be submitting the test and sharing your opinion regarding the revisions (Usually 3 days).

Regarding the budget, we are paying a fixed fee of $300 for the revisions. Based on the scope and requirements, we believe this is a fair compensation for the project.

Thank you once again! Looking forward to hearing from you.

source_message.text:
Hi Jessica,

We liked your test submission, and we'd love to have you on board to help us update our Leadership Interview Questions You'll Most Likely Be Asked book!

To make sure we're aligned from the start, we wanted to walk you through the full scope of the project so you have a clear picture of what's ahead.

**Project Aim**

We're looking to update the first edition of the Leadership Interview Questions book so it reflects current industry standards and feels relevant to today's readers. As a quick-reference guide for interview preparation, this book is aimed at managers, team leads, and senior professionals with 4 to 5+ years of experience, as well as those stepping into leadership roles for the first time. We'd also like the book to offer a global perspective — showing how questions and answers can vary by country and industry.

**Project Stages**

**1\. Reviewing and updating existing content (Milestone 1)**
We'll share the first edition with you to review. As you go through the 250 questions, we'd love your input on which ones might be removed — whether because they feel outdated, don't quite connect with today's leadership landscape, or overlap with other questions in the book.

\--Streamlining the question set based on your review

\--Developing answers for the remaining content — worth noting, the answer layers we discussed (interviewer's intent, common mistakes, how to structure the answer, and answer framework) may not apply to every question. Once we've finalized the question set together, we can decide which ones need the full set of layers and which need just a couple.

**2\. Adding new chapters (Milestone 2)**
We're hoping to introduce a few new sections/chapters, and would love your thoughts on shaping them:

\--Pre-interview preparation checklist — since this audience already has experience, this chapter may need a leadership-specific angle rather than the basics. If there are tips especially relevant to leadership-level interviews, we'd love to include those.

\--Remote & Hybrid Leadership questions

\--Questions candidates can ask the interviewer

\--How to use AI for interview preparation (prompts, techniques, tools)

\--Questions specifically geared toward first-time leaders

Based on your response to the last briefing, you have highlighted which chapters seem the most relevant, and that's great! However, we are expecting all the chapters to be short only unless they include question & answer. The AI chapter seemed the most unique advantage that we could provide to the readers. In the current landscape, learning how to use AI for different purposes is important. So, that chapter has to be there.

**3\. Hybrid Experience (Milestone 3)**

\--All our books aim to offer readers a hybrid learning experience, since not everyone wants to read cover-to-cover. Alongside the book, we'd like to offer companion online resources — checklists, AI prompts, videos on body language, mock interviews, answer templates, leadership resume tips, or any other ideas you might have.

**A Note on Word Count**

As you work through the review and new additions, we'd appreciate you keeping an eye on the overall word count. Our books cap at 50K words, and the first edition sits around 37K — so on paper, that leaves roughly 13K words of room. That said, since we're revising the book fairly thoroughly and removing some questions along the way, we're hopeful that will free up additional space. Just wanted to flag that the final word count shouldn't go beyond 50K overall.

We've also attached our author guidelines for the Interview series — please take a look and let us know if anything needs more clarity. Link to author guidelines: <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qd2L4HTm9ySBm41Z-XmrBeDS5Vga15Xyzpqwv0l2SIM/edit?usp=sharing>

Finally, here's the link to the full book in a Google Doc format. We're using the Google Doc version to track changes, though we're happy to share a PDF as well if that's easier for reference: <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1R_MeiYyX-mng1SXf25i6WdQpxfVEpyxILbL0NoaDbkw/edit?usp=sharing>

The actual working manuscript will be shared once we begin the project and make changes accordingly.

Looking forward to working on this together, Jessica — please don't hesitate to reach out with any questions! And if you would like to get on a call to clear your doubts, we can schedule a call accordingly.

value_updates.audience_focus: leadership-specific preparation for experienced candidates rather than basic interview preparation

Hi Jessica,

For Milestone 1:

\- Yes, we agree that cutting down the questions is the right choice. We would really appreciate it if you could provide short reasons for the questions you remove. You can comment directly on the Google Doc we've shared with you — simply delete the questions you want to remove and add a comment explaining the reasoning. (Please note that we won't be able to provide a downloadable copy of the document at this stage. We've given you commenting access so you can delete in suggesting mode while leaving a comment with your reasoning.)

Once the questions list is finalized, we will create a working manuscript containing only the final questions, so it's easier to build on those specifically.

\- Regarding the layers of the answers: we think every question should have at least two layers — how to frame the answer, and a sample answer. Layers like interviewer's intent, common mistakes, and framework may not apply to every question.

\- The target deadline for this milestone will be part of the overall project timeline.

For Milestone 2: New Chapters

\- By "global perspective," we don't mean dedicating specific chapters to it, but rather weaving it naturally into the existing chapters. For example, for a pre-interview checklist, the process might differ between the USA and India, or the way answers are framed might differ between the US and the UK. A brief note at the beginning would work well — clarifying that the book's primary focus is the US and Indian audience, but that additional tips are included throughout to highlight how a global perspective may differ, where relevant.

We'd also welcome your suggestions on which other markets we should keep in mind, apart from the US and India.

\- We don't have a fixed target, but as a rough estimate, each chapter should ideally fall between 2.5k and 3.5k words. It can be shorter or slightly longer depending on the topic and the depth it requires. Ideally, for an interview questions book, chapters focused on theory should be kept relatively short.

For Milestone 3: Hybrid Companion Resources

\- This phase is part of the overall project and should ideally be completed within the allotted project timeline. That said, the milestones won't run in parallel — they'll proceed step by step, with each one beginning only after the previous is complete. So the third milestone will begin once the manuscript work is nearly finished.

\- For the hybrid resources, most assets should ideally be finished products. However, for video ideas, you can provide the script, and we'll handle the recording on our end. Templates will need to be prepared by you so the production team can create exactly what you have in mind.

The examples we shared for the hybrid resources are ones we believe will give the book an edge over others in the market, while also helping readers learn visually and practically rather than relying solely on the text. We'd also love to hear your suggestions on what you think would make a great companion to this kind of book.

General Queries

Regarding the compensation structure: The total compensation for the project is $300, and we are planning to split it across three milestones of $100 each, based on the completion of the agreed deliverables at each stage. However, if you have a different milestone structure in mind, we're happy to discuss it and see what works best for both of us.

Contract: Yes, absolutely. We will be sending over the contract once we have finalized the details and are ready to move forward with the project.

The target date for the final manuscript is one month from the project start date; however, we're flexible on this. Now that you have a full picture of the project's scope and requirements, please let us know what timeline you'd be comfortable working with. The milestone breakdown that we have provided is the ideal from our perspective, but if you wish to share your own milestone breakdown, please do so. We can discuss that accordingly.

Throughout the process, there will be scheduled review periods during which our editorial team will share feedback.

If you have any further questions or need more clarity on any of the points above, please don't hesitate to let us know. We'd be happy to hop on a call to discuss everything in detail so we're both fully aligned.

Alongside the book, we'd like to offer companion online resources — checklists, AI prompts, videos on body language, mock interviews, answer templates, leadership resume tips, or any other ideas you might have.

The overall word count of the book should be 50k. So, the author should stay within that word count limit and plan the content around it.

The author is free to suggest any other revisions or additions they think would make the book highly relevant or interactive to the current audience. However, the implementation of those ideas will happen after a discussion with the editorial team.

\-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Please confirm that you are clear on the above requirements for this project and are okay with moving ahead.

Regarding the contract, our team is finalizing the contract, and we’ll be sharing it with you soon for your review.

Thank you for your patience! We look forward to working with you on this project and getting started as soon as possible.

source_message.text:
Hi Jessica,

Thank you for the time you've put into Milestones 1 and 2. After a thorough review, our editorial team has identified concerns that we need to raise with you directly.

**Leftover instructional text:** Milestone 1 includes a note at the top with direct usage instructions ("delete or edit the question in suggesting mode... then paste the comment as your rationale") — scaffolding from an AI workflow that appears to have been left in by mistake.

**A reference to nonexistent content:** The document and the text in the manuscript refer to a "book-wide note on the first page," which does not actually appear anywhere in the document.

**Turnaround time:** Milestone 2 — five full chapters — was submitted within roughly one day, which isn't consistent with the depth of original analysis this work requires.

**AI-detection results:** Independent tools flagged Milestone 2 content in the 75–90% range.

Your contract permits limited AI-assisted tools for spelling, grammar, research, outlining, translation, and editorial support, provided the final manuscript reflects your own original work and professional judgment. Based on the observations above, the submitted material does not appear to meet that condition.

Taking all of this into account, we won't be moving forward with this project. We appreciate your interest in the role and the effort you put in, and we wish you the best going forward.

Thank you.

routing_warnings.description: The client's findings about AI-assisted content and insufficient original professional judgment are execution evidence for the original-authorship Requirement, while the project-termination clause supports removal of the target chapter Requirement.
